en.headline: Journalists raise concerns as government tightens media access to land records
en.dek: Subsidiary legislation tabled at the Legislative Council would require journalists to apply for searches on public-interest grounds, with the Land Registrar deciding case by case.
body: The Hong Kong Journalists Association and some lawmakers have expressed concern about plans to tighten arrangements for searching land records, after the government tabled related subsidiary legislation at the Legislative Council.

The Land Titles Regulation and other items were presented for negative vetting. Most provisions, including the search changes, are due to take effect in the first half of next year. Under the proposed rules, searches generally require one of nine specified purposes. News reporting is not listed as a standalone purpose.

Journalists seeking access for public-interest reasons would need to apply separately. The Land Registrar would consider each application individually. The association said the changes had not been adequately justified or consulted on, and warned they could reduce the public’s ability to monitor the property market.
Some legislators have asked the government to clarify the operational details and to streamline the process so that investigative reporting is not unduly affected.

zh.headline: 政府收緊土地查冊安排 傳媒及議員表示關注
zh.dek: 相關附屬法例已提交立法會先訂立後審議，傳媒若以公眾利益為由查冊須個別申請，由土地註冊處處長考慮。
body: 政府向立法會提交相關附屬法例後，香港記者協會及部分議員對收緊土地查冊安排表示關注。
有關法例以先訂立後審議形式提交，大部分條文包括查冊改動預計於明年上半年生效。新安排下，查冊一般須符合九項指明目的之一，新聞報道並非獨立列明的目的。
傳媒若以公眾利益為由查冊，需另行申請，由土地註冊處處長個別考慮。記協指當局未有充分解釋或諮詢，並擔心會削弱公眾監察物業市場的能力。
部分議員要求政府澄清運作細節，並簡化申請程序，以免影響調查報道。
